intervals.locator: end: PandaX collaboration slides, 2026/07/16, slide "Current Status"
intervals.note: The collaboration slides of 16 July 2026 give "Shut down at Apr. 15th"; the Run 2 physics data period ended earlier, "from July 5, 2024, to January 23, 2026" (arXiv:2607.02405). Run 1 ran 2021/11-2022/05 per the same slides, followed by a hall renovation at CJPL (2022/09-2023/12) during which the detector was not taking data; this interval is not split at that gap.

intervals.label: PandaX-4T operation concluded (shut down)
intervals.note: Terminal event. Day from a collaboration talk slide (secondary); the CPS abstract says only that the experiment "concluded its operation and was decommissioned in May 2026". The successor PandaX-20T (xenon transferred to CJPL; "2028.1: PandaX-20T physics operation") is not an Atlas entity yet.

intervals.label: PandaX-4T decommissioned
intervals.locator: CPS HEP annual meeting abstract, 17 July 2026; slides: "Now: 4T has been diamantled [sic], 20T Xenon transferred to CJPL"
intervals.quote: After completing three data-taking runs, the PandaX-4T experiment concluded its operation and was decommissioned in May 2026.

name: PandaX-4T
notes: external.inspire_experiment (1221671) is the umbrella INSPIRE experiment record for the whole PandaX programme (legacy_name "PandaX"); no PandaX-4T-specific INSPIRE experiment record was found via an inspirehep.net query on 2026-09-17.

The official site's "4-ton sensitive target" (design) and the commissioning-run paper's "3.7-tonne of liquid xenon target" (the actual target mass used in that specific analysis) are both recorded as separate key_specs rather than merged, since they describe different things (design capacity vs. an as-run analysis mass).

The detector phase (single-phase or dual-phase) is not recorded: no source consulted used the words "dual-phase" or "two-phase" for PandaX-4T specifically (checked directly), even though PandaX-4T is understood elsewhere to be a dual-phase xenon TPC like its siblings LZ/XENONnT. The phase is left unsourced rather than assumed.

physics_goals.quote: With 6-ton of total Xenon and 4-ton sensitive target, PandaX-4T aims to improve the dark matter sensitivity by one order of magnitude
value: Detect or exclude WIMP dark matter scattering off xenon nuclei with a 4-tonne sensitive target

summary.plain: PandaX-4T is a dark matter detector holding four tonnes of liquid xenon, deep under a mountain at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. It has been taking data since 2021, searching for dark matter particles bumping into xenon nuclei.
summary.technical: Dual-target-scale xenon TPC (6 t total xenon inventory, 4 t sensitive target) at CJPL-II, 2400 m underground. Commissioned 2021; the commissioning-run result (3.7 t target, 0.63 t-y exposure) excluded spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross sections above 3.8 × 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² at 40 GeV/c² (90% CL).
